header.userPrompt:
Speed up the server test suite by using a SINGLE shared Postgres container for the entire test run,
instead of today's per-test container. Server TEST code only — do NOT change production code.

PROBLEM: `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/core/PostgresSpec.scala` extends
`com.dimafeng.testcontainers.scalatest.TestContainerForEach`, so EVERY test starts a fresh `postgres:13`
container, runs `CREATE EXTENSION CITEXT`, and `Evolutions.applyEvolutions(...)`, then tears it down.
With ~67 specs this is hundreds of serialized container start/evolve/stop cycles and dominates the suite
(and CI) runtime.

GOAL: one Postgres container started ONCE for the whole test JVM and shared by ALL server specs, with
evolutions applied ONCE against it. Because the DB is now shared and NOT reset between tests, tests must
isolate themselves with RANDOM, user-scoped data rather than relying on a pristine/empty DB.

BUILD:
1. Shared singleton container:
   - Introduce a single long-lived `postgres:13` container started once per test JVM (e.g. a lazy
     `object SharedPostgres`), with `CREATE EXTENSION CITEXT` and `Evolutions.applyEvolutions` run exactly
     once against it (guard so repeated access does not re-run them). Do NOT stop it per test/suite — let
     it live for the JVM (Ryuk / a shutdown hook cleans it up).
   - Rework `PostgresSpec` so `withDatabase` returns the shared `Database` (no per-test container). Keep the
     same `withDatabase[T](runTest: Database => T): T` signature so repository specs need no call-site
     change beyond data isolation.
   - Rework the controller/Play base the same way: the `guiceApplicationBuilder(container)` specs must build
     their Play app against the SHARED container's JDBC url (point the DB config at the singleton), not a
     per-test container. Evolutions are already applied to the shared DB; Play's startup evolutions must not
     fight that (they are idempotent once applied).
2. Test isolation via random data (the behavioral change):
   - Add a small test helper for unique random values (e.g. `randomEmail()`, `randomName()`, random strings)
     and use it wherever a test inserts rows with UNIQUE columns (emails, names, etc.). Entity ids are
     already UUIDv7 (unique) — keep using fresh ids per test.
   - Every test must create and assert on ITS OWN data, scoped to its own user. Remove assumptions that the
     DB is empty or globally small: no "the table has exactly N rows", no "list returns all X across the
     whole DB", no asserting on global counts. Scope list/count assertions to the test's own user or the
     specific rows it created (presence/shape, not global totals).
3. Fix the fallout, not every spec blindly:
   - Implement the shared container, run the full server suite, and FIX the specs that now fail under
     sharing — collisions on unique columns (switch to random values) and global-state assertions (scope
     them). Specs that are already user-scoped and use fresh ids may need no change. Do not weaken an
     assertion beyond scoping it to the test's own data.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Server TEST sources only (`server/src/test`). No production code change. No new DB evolution. No
  dependency changes (testcontainers is already present); revert incidental yarn.lock churn.
- Keep `Test / fork := true` for server. Do NOT enable cross-run container reuse (`withReuse` /
  testcontainers.reuse) — that is for local dev and risks stale state in CI. This change is a single
  container per RUN, not persisted across runs.
- Do NOT change test parallelism settings in this PR (correctness of the shared-container + random-data
  model first; parallelism can be a follow-up).
- Follow docs/guide/testing.md. Attribution: NO Claude session links in commits or the PR description;
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude` IS allowed.

VERIFY:
- The full server suite passes with a single shared container: confirm (via logs) that the container is
  started once, not per test. Targeted `sbt "testOnly *Spec"` while iterating; the final stage runs the
  whole suite (`CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test`).
- Do not regress coverage — the same specs run, only their data setup/isolation changes.
